title: Пантелеев А.В. 2001. Список птиц Новгородской области // Русский орнитологический журнал. Экспресс-выпуск 141: 331-343
use: Regional bird checklist with literature per species since Петров 1885 (Приильменье). Presence in Novgorod region (modern/19th c.); no status/abundance.

title: Мальчевский А.С., Пукинский Ю.Б. 1983. Птицы Ленинградской области и сопредельных территорий. Л.: Изд-во ЛГУ. Т. 1-2 (электронная версия zoomet.ru, по видам)
use: Per-species status (resident/migrant/passage), abundance words, arrival/departure, voice and nesting for NW Russia incl. Novgorod region. Species page URL is given in each bird row (malchevsky_page). Extracted by scripts/extract-malchevsky.py keyword digest; statements are modern (XIX-XX c.) and applied to 1230 as analogy.

title: Звери Вологодской области (Вологда, после 1957; ред. В. К. Пудожгорский; автор на сайте не указан). Полный текст, booksite.ru
use: Species accounts for mammals of the adjacent north-east of the historical Novgorod land (Белоозеро): activity, hibernation, moult, dens, nests, tracks, fur trade. Modern analogue.

title: Валдайский национальный парк. Животные парка (официальный сайт)
use: Modern mammal and bird composition inside Novgorod oblast (Валдай): >45 mammal species, 217 bird species; rare/Red Book species; synanthropes. Modern analogue only.

title: Фауна. Новгородская область (nbcrs.org, популярный региональный обзор)
use: Modern common/rare mammals of Novgorod oblast; acclimatised sika deer and raccoon dog; 11 mammal and 48 bird species in the regional Red Book. Popular source: used only for modern status and anachronism checks.

title: Рыбина Е.А. 2015. Промыслы в средневековом Новгороде (по археологическим материалам)
use: Birch-bark letters XII-XV c.: белка most frequent; куница 7 letters; бобр 5; песец, заяц, лисица, выдра, соболь, нерпа, росомаха once each; hides of elk, deer, bear. Bone-tipped blunt arrows (томары, ~120) used for valuable fur animals (sable, marten, stoat); wooden arrows >350 in X-XII c.; a whole ash hunting bow, XIII c. (WK claim:agriculture-fauna-ash-hunting-bow).

title: Hamilton-Dyer S., Brisbane M., Maltby M. 2017. Fish, feather, fur and forest: Exploitation of wild animals in medieval Novgorod and its territory // Quaternary International 460: 97-107
use: Via WK research environment-agriculture-fauna.md FAU-02/FAU-04 and search abstract: wild mammals small dietary share; hare, beaver and elk most frequent wild bones; very few fur-bearer bones (bear claws, squirrel, marten, otter, fox, beaver); falconry attested in the territory.

title: Maltby M., Hamilton-Dyer S., Zinoviev A.V., Sablin M. 2020. The exploitation of wild mammals in Novgorod and sites in its immediate hinterland // Animals and Archaeology in Northern Medieval Russia. Oxbow: 223-237
use: Search abstract only: 106 beaver from Troitsky sites, foot bones under-represented (skins), 35% butchery marks.

title: Elk in Medieval Towns of Rus': Meat, Hides, and Antler Economies // International Journal of Osteoarchaeology (2025)
use: Search abstract only: elk ~0.2% of identified mammal bones in medieval Novgorod, one third butchered, antler pedicles removed.

title: Zinoviev A.V. 2025. When Synanthropic Birds Appeared in Medieval Novgorod the Great and Tver (Russia): Historical and Zooarchaeological Accounts // Int. J. Osteoarchaeology 35: 89-96
use: Abstract (also WK claim:urban-bird-period-specific): corvids (raven, hooded crow, rook, jackdaw) and pigeon early urban adapters; feral pigeon and tree sparrow documented by the 13th c.; magpie and starling later-medieval colonisers of the town.

title: 53 Новости: «Зоолог рассказал историю заселения Новгорода птицами» (популярное изложение работы А.В. Зиновьева)
use: Hooded crow and raven from X c.; rooks colonies from XI c.; pigeon X c.; magpie bones not found in Novgorod. States starling appeared in XIII c. — conflicts with the abstract (later-medieval); conflict kept in notes.

title: Зиновьев А.В. 2012. Орлан-белохвост: история взаимодействия с человеком в Евразии (по археозоологическим материалам) // Труды VI Междунар. конф. по соколообразным и совам Северной Евразии: 26-30
use: White-tailed eagle tarsometatarsus from Десятинный раскоп, Novgorod, late XI - early XII c.; eagles scavenge at refuse heaps at settlement edges; wing feathers used for arrow fletching; hunting with eagles extremely rare.

title: Зиновьев А.В. 2011. Птицы средневекового Новгорода Великого (X–XIV вв.): фаунистический состав и хозяйственное значение // Новгород и Новгородская земля. История и археология. Т. 25: 277-287
use: Bibliographic only (cited in SRC_ZIN2012). Not read; the full Novgorod bird bone list is a GAP.

title: Gorobets L., Kovalchuk O. 2017. Birds in the medieval culture and economy of the East Slavs in the 10-13th centuries AD // Environmental Archaeology 22(2)
use: Search abstract: primary game birds ducks, geese, swans, common crane, corvids, plus black grouse and capercaillie in forest zone; goshawk the most popular bird of prey (falconry); Novgorod region: 77 capercaillie and 10 black grouse bones; feathers used for arrows.

title: WK claims from Hamilton-Dyer 2002 «The Bird Resources of Medieval Novgorod» (Acta Zool. Cracov. 45: 99-107)
use: claim:environment-p1-bird-taxa (chicken and ducks most frequent identified bird remains; mallard not always separable from domestic duck); claim:environment-p1-wildfowl-season (wild bird take depended largely on seasonal arrivals).
